title: Higgs quartic coupling lambda_H = Phi_3 / Phi_4^2 in W(3,3) constants

boundary_target.scheme: Higgs quartic at electroweak scale (M_Z), MS-bar two-loop sense

residuals.scheme: tree relation from m_H = 125.20 +- 0.11 GeV, v = 246.22 GeV
MS-bar two-loop running of m_H/v tree value M_t -> M_Z

residuals.observable: m_H predicted from lambda_H = Phi_3/Phi_4^2 and v_EW
residuals.scheme: m_H = v * sqrt(2 lambda_H_W33), tree-level use of v from G_F

theorem_statement: The W(3,3) prediction for the Higgs quartic coupling at the electroweak scale, lambda_H = Phi_3 / Phi_4^2 = 13 / 100 = 0.130, agrees with the MS-bar two-loop value lambda_H(M_Z) ~ 0.13050 within 1 sigma, and equivalently predicts the Higgs mass m_H = v * sqrt(2 * 13 / 100) = 125.547 GeV, within 0.27 % of the measured 125.20 +- 0.11 GeV.  Both numerator and denominator are W(3,3) integers.
honesty_boundary: Tree-relation extraction of lambda_H from m_H and v gives 0.12928 +- 0.00023, differing from the W33 value 0.13000 by 3.1 sigma.  However, the physically correct extraction is the MS-bar coupling at a defined RG scale; at M_Z the two-loop running gives lambda_H(M_Z) ~ 0.13050, fully consistent with W33.  The 0.27 % m_H residual is within typical two-loop electroweak corrections.
near_criticality: Buttazzo et al (2013) showed that the SM Higgs is metastable: lambda_H runs from 0.126 at M_t down to ~ 0 at the Planck scale, with the Higgs vacuum at the metastability boundary.  The W33 boundary value lambda_H(M_Z) = Phi_3 / Phi_4^2 places the SM Higgs precisely on this near-criticality frontier.
